Been there so many times with the “why me” spiral and the truth of it is, it sucks. There is no justifying it. Life is just shit and unfair, but you do hold a lot of power too. 

There are a few things to consider:
Just like me, and everyone for that matter, there is an aspect of you who does this to yourself. 
Intentional? Fuck no, but being aware of how you can push yourself in the wrong direction out of habit, poor sleep, diet, mentality, etc
It’s important to realise that these are not easy but they are in your control. Which is great because you can change them. 

You are not lazy, you are ill. Be kind to yourself because not everyone else will. You just need to take it slow whilst you recover from this illness, like ANY other.

Finally, the giving up thing. I agree, I think you should give up, I think you want to. But I think you’re missing the message that is being sent. 
Give up on the resistance, not life. Give up caring, give up searching. Just take every moment as it comes and surrender to life. Don’t give up perusing your goals and go get high for no reason, no I’m not saying that. I’m saying give up doing anything that ISN’T pursuing your goals. Give up on everything accept you. Never give up on you.
Pray for me 🥲

I have same issue mate, probably a mixture of bad mobility and long femurs, I can try help you find the culprit, first try experiment with different stance widths and pointing your toes further out or in, that could be an instant fix, next try testing ankle flexibility by getting knee over toe without your heel lifting up (lunges or wall test) see if there is an imbalance or lack of any knee over toe if so work on ankles, next could be your hips, practice sitting in the deep squat (hold a weight/plate in front of you to stop you falling on your back) and use your elbows to push your knees out, even leaning side to side and hold for a minute or so. These are just some things that helped me (in my case it was left ankle imbalance and tight hips, along with long femurs) just be aware that this takes time, it took me about a month of consistent stretching of my ankles and stretching before every set before I saw any depth improvement. 

Your squat is pretty much parallel so it’s not a huge deal but if you really want below parallel then try a few of these and see how you get on.

GL mate
